title: Infra behind Krea 2: How to train and serve at scale — Gabriel Jorge Menezes, Krea.ai
talk_summary: Gabriel Menezes describes Krea's infrastructure for training and serving their image model: a single GPU cluster shared between training and inference, with a queue (Kueue) for gang-scheduled training jobs, virtual-kubelet to burst inference to external providers, and taint/descheduler logic to reclaim GPUs. The main transferable lessons are about observability, checkpointing, and letting the scheduler handle failures rather than hand-fixing them.

takeaways.technique: Let the orchestrator handle failures; don't hand-rescue
takeaways.what_they_do: When a pod or remote job fails, they mark it failed and let Kubernetes recreate it rather than debugging each failure manually; they also learned to just let flaky runs crash and retry on the same machines.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just mark it as failed, let Kubernetes handle it, create a new one, and things keep working

takeaways.technique: Priority queue with gang scheduling for heavy jobs
takeaways.what_they_do: Researchers submit jobs to a queue (Kueue) with workload priority; gang scheduling ensures a training job gets all its resources at once or waits, and production is lower priority than training.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It does gang scheduling. Gang scheduling is important for for for trainings in general.

takeaways.what_they_do: When GPUs are free in the cluster they taint nodes so external-provider pods don't schedule there; when training takes the GPUs, the taint is removed and a descheduler slowly migrates pods back so production doesn't drop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this system my like slowly migrates the pods back, so production doesn't go down and we don't waste money

takeaways.technique: Invest in metrics that reflect real work, not vanity utilization
takeaways.what_they_do: They found GPU utilization misleading and switched to tensor-core utilization plus InfiniBand/NVLink error metrics, which caught most of their cross-node failures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is GPU utilization which is a lie. Uh, don't trust this.

takeaways.technique: Frequent checkpointing to survive constant crashes
takeaways.what_they_do: Because runs crashed every few hours, they checkpointed every 20-30 minutes to a fast filesystem so a crash cost little progress.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we could checkpoint every like 30 minutes, 20 minutes, produce like a terabyte of data in like less than 30 seconds
takeaways.numbers: checkpoint every 20-30 min; ~1.8 TB/s reads, ~1 TB/s writes

takeaways.technique: Hide infrastructure from workers via a queue
takeaways.what_they_do: Researchers just submit jobs; a queue decides when GPUs are available, so nobody thinks about capacity and work isn't delayed by production.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I don't want my researchers to think about GPUs. I just want them to launch stuff and this goes into a queue
